docs.text:
MCAP Ops is a standalone Rust library with NumPy interfaces for inspecting recordings and preparing model inputs. Preserve the clock, the validity mask, and the source support alongside every value.

Current interface: 0.1.0. Install from source; there is no PyPI or crates.io release. Core works with arrays independently of MCAP, ROS, and robot schemas. CDR/Protobuf decoding, dataset writing, scheduling, and clock estimation belong to upstream adapters. See installation and verified platforms.

docs.title: Architecture and Design
docs.text: Documentation · Data contracts · Operators

docs.title: Composable processing, explicit policy
docs.text:
A recording can serve quality review, training-data conversion, and debugging. The library provides deterministic computation and evidence. Upstream applications own topic meaning, units, coordinate frames, task success criteria, and action semantics. MCAP sources are read-only; transformations create new values without rewriting original timestamps or source data.

An operator here is a function with an explicit input/output contract, such as Signal -> QualityReport. It is not necessarily a GPU kernel, matrix operation, or independently scheduled node.

Core is an independent crate. Rust applications can use it without IO. Python bindings depend on both crates; IO uses core's Signal, while core never depends on IO.

docs.title: Detection, selection, transformation
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    S["Original Signal"] --> Q["inspect_signal<br/>Detect"]
    Q --> E["QualityReport<br/>Evidence"]
    E --> G["gate / upstream policy<br/>Decide"]
    G --> I["IntervalSet / upstream mask<br/>Select"]
    S --> T["resample / fir / ema<br/>Transform"]
    I -->|"Caller chooses processing intervals"| T
    T --> O["New values + validity / provenance"]

Detection reports candidates without repairing them. Gating makes decisions without deleting files. Selection does not concatenate disjoint segments into apparently continuous time. Transformations retain invalidity rather than inventing zero observations. Callers compose these functions; there is no hidden DAG executor.

docs.title: Schema decoding is an extension point
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    F["MCAP file"] --> R["RawReader<br/>Original order / Limits / CRC"]
    R --> J["JsonSignalSpec<br/>JSON Pointer"]
    R --> D["User SignalDecoder<br/>CDR / Protobuf / Other"]
    J --> S["Signal"]
    D --> S
    U["Existing upstream decoder"] --> A["NumPy arrays or Rust Signal"]
    A --> C["Core operators"]
    S --> C

Built-in JSON extraction requires message_encoding=json. Unknown payloads remain inspectable as containers and raw messages; they are not guessed into numeric arrays. The Rust trait takes &mcap::Message and returns a Vec<DecodedSample>, allowing an adapter to explicitly expand batched samples. There is no dynamic plugin registry or Python callback-decoder interface.

docs.title: Ownership and performance
docs.text:
1. Python timestamps must be contiguous int64; values may be one- or two-dimensional float64 arrays, including strided views.
  2. Each call creates a Rust-owned input snapshot. Outputs do not alias caller buffers; ownership does not depend on the caller retaining an input view.
  3. Numeric outputs go directly to NumPy. Owned buffers transfer when supported; small diagnostic reports still pass through JSON.
  4. Bindings currently hold the GIL. There is no global thread pool; episode-level process scheduling belongs upstream.
  5. Start by eliminating repeated traversals, allocations, sorting, and conversion. Introduce additional paths only when benchmarks justify them.
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Python caller
    participant P as PyO3 boundary
    participant C as Rust core
    U->>P: int64 time + float64 values + configuration
    P->>P: Validate and create owned snapshot
    P->>C: Signal + options
    C-->>P: Sampled / Filtered / Report
    P-->>U: NumPy arrays / dictionary, no input aliases

IO does not imply constant memory: chunks require decompression, read_signal collects selected values, and inspect_mcap retains selected timestamps. Callers must choose appropriate record, message, and decoded-sample limits.

docs.title: Integration boundaries
docs.text:
Providers define fields, units, frames, joint order, commands, and clock mappings. The operator library does not guess whether an action is absolute, relative, or a controller target. LeTools/converters own UI, episode boundaries, train/validation splits, dataset writing, and publication.

Image metrics describe luminance, exposure, and Laplacian variance, not learned quality scores. Video validation checks complete decoding of the first video stream; it does not establish semantic quality or reconstruct packet timestamps.

Not implemented: automatic clock fitting, universal CDR/Protobuf decoding, a web UI, dataset writers, GPU operators, or GIL release. Add future capabilities at explicit seams with their own contracts and validation.

docs.title: Data Contracts and Abstractions
docs.text: Documentation · Architecture · Python API

docs.title: Signal: values travel with time
docs.text:
timestamps: int64[N]       nanoseconds; the caller identifies the clock
values:     float64[N, D]  N samples, D channels

row 0: t0 -> [x0, y0, z0]
row 1: t1 -> [x1, y1, z1]
row 2: t2 -> [x2, y2, z2]

Rust stores flat row-major values. Python accepts (N,) or (N,D) and returns Signal values as two-dimensional arrays. Input dtypes are not corrected implicitly. Timestamps, targets, centers, and offsets must be contiguous; values may be strided or reversed, retaining logical order. Python numeric outputs normalize non-finite values to NaN; do not assume a Rust Inf remains Inf after crossing that boundary.

Signal::new checks shape only, allowing quality inspection to see disorder and NaN/Inf. Each transformation validates its own preconditions. Sampling, EMA, and FIR require strictly increasing source timestamps.

SignalSpec is caller-held metadata, not embedded policy. Units and frames are not converted automatically. A max_rate threshold uses value-units/second; max_acceleration uses value-units/second squared.

docs.title: Time is not an ordinary floating-point axis
docs.text:
• Core timestamps are signed int64 nanoseconds; out-of-range MCAP u64 timestamps fail conversion.
  • Selection intervals are half-open [start_ns,end_ns). An Issue's last_ns instead includes the final source sample.
  • uniform_grid uses rational rate_num/rate_den Hz and integer arithmetic, avoiding floating-point epoch accumulation.
  • map_clock takes an explicit origin, offset, and ppb correction. It does not estimate clock offsets or sensor response delay.
  • Inspect original ordering before deciding to sort, deduplicate, or segment. Sorting first can hide a clock reversal.

docs.title: Inspection, gating, and selection
docs.text:
Issue contains code, optional channel, [start_index,end_index_exclusive), start_ns, last_ns, metric, and threshold. It currently has no severity field; upstream policy assigns severity.

QualityReport contains time, channels, issues, total_issues, issues_truncated, flagged_sample_count, and dynamic_checks_completed. Some dynamic checks are skipped when timestamps are not strictly increasing; the absence of rate/spike issues then does not prove normal data.

Issue detail is capped at max_issues while total counts and flagged fractions remain available. Python does not serialize the internal flagged_samples or all_codes, and does not export gate. Do not reconstruct a supposedly complete bad-sample mask from truncated issue detail. Rust gate uses the full internal statistics.

IntervalSet represents selection. affected_centers(history_ns,future_ns) expands bad intervals to target centers whose context overlaps them. Preserve segment boundaries rather than pretending disconnected selections are continuous.

docs.title: Resampling: values, validity, source support
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Source a<br/>0 ms / 0.0"] --> C["Target<br/>5 ms / 0.5"]
    B["Source b<br/>10 ms / 1.0"] --> C
    C --> D["left=0 / right=1<br/>alpha=0.5 / uses_future=true"]
Method Behavior Required policy previous Latest source sample at or before the target max_age_ns; bounded holding after the final source is allowed nearest Closest source sample; ties prefer the past allow_future and max_age_ns linear Linear interpolation between finite supports max_gap_ns; off-grid values normally need future support slerp Shortest-path xyzw quaternion interpolation Four channels; input norm within 0.01 of one, then normalized internally

max_gap_ns bounds the span between two interpolation supports. max_age_ns bounds the distance to a single matched sample. Both default to zero, normally permitting only exact matches. Linear/SLERP do not extrapolate; previous/nearest may retain an endpoint within the age limit. Exact source matches can remain valid at the endpoints of an otherwise unsupported gap.

Code Name Meaning 0 Valid Supported result 1 Missing No usable support 2 Gap Interpolation support span exceeds the limit 3 Stale Single-sample support exceeds the age limit 4 NonFinite Non-finite support or computed output 5 Future Future support required but prohibited 6 InvalidQuaternion Quaternion requirements are not met

Invalid values are NaN, source indices are -1, and alpha is NaN. Check valid before indexing; Python's -1 would otherwise select the last array entry. uses_future is populated for successful outputs, so False alone does not prove validity. Validity is row-wise, not per channel: a non-finite required channel invalidates the sampled row.

docs.title: History windows and causality
docs.text:
model center = 20 ms
offsets      = [-15, -10, -5, 0] ms
request time = [  5,  10, 15, 20] ms

values.shape     = (T, W, D)
timestamps.shape = (T, W)
valid.shape      = (T * W,)      current Python API; reshape explicitly

Centers are strictly increasing. Offsets are nonempty, strictly increasing, and nonpositive. status, source_left/right, alpha, and uses_future are also flat (T*W,), ordered by center first.

Nonpositive offsets constrain requested times, not necessarily source supports. With linear, allow_future=True, a request may consume a source after that request or even after the model center. Use previous or prohibit future support for strict online features, and inspect the returned status.

docs.title: Filtering is separate from resampling
docs.text:
EMA uses actual dt and a time constant in seconds, resetting after gaps or non-finite rows. FIR requires a regular period within tolerance, does not pad unsupported edges, and invalidates support crossing gaps.

lowpass_taps only creates coefficients; resample does not automatically anti-alias. Before downsampling, choose a lowpass based on the new Nyquist limit and process supported continuous segments.

Mode lookahead_samples group_delay_samples EMA 0 None; frequency-dependent Symmetric causal FIR 0 (tap_count-1)/2 Centered FIR tap_count/2 0 in output alignment; requires future support Asymmetric causal FIR 0 None

Python EMA/FIR valid is currently list[bool]; convert with np.asarray for array operations. Filters do not shift timestamps to compensate for delay. Angle unwrapping is explicit and should not be applied to every numeric channel.

docs.title: Errors and provenance
docs.text:
Invalid arguments, overflow, bad shape, and invalid ordering fail explicitly. Representable per-sample missing support returns status instead. Python core, image, and video failures mainly map to ValueError; MCAP read/decode failures map to OSError. Binding-level dtype mismatches may raise TypeError.

Provenance is not a complete lineage database. Sampled retains interpolation support, and MCAP reports retain source/version/schema identity. Upstream applications should also retain file identity, decoder configuration, clock mapping, selection policy, and operator version. Image rgb_sha256 hashes dimensions and decoded RGB content, not the original compressed file.

docs.title: Contributing, Validation, and Publication
docs.text: Documentation · Repository rules · RSI

docs.title: Separate authoring from execution
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["Author and review locally"] --> B["Synchronize relative source paths"]
    B --> C["Linux execution environment<br/>Build and test"]
    C --> D["Commit locally"]
    D --> E["Git bundle + tracked-file hashes"]
    E --> F["Verified remote fast-forward"]
    F --> G["Push reviewed history"]

Use an isolated Linux x86-64 execution checkout with project-local Rust/Python tooling. The historical reference environment used 32 logical CPU threads, a fixed performance-core affinity, Rust 1.90.0, and a release build. See the performance guide for the full reproducibility conditions. A different environment needs its own validation, not a claim of identical speed.

Do not publish deployment aliases, account names, absolute workspace paths, or boot identifiers. Supply execution coordinates through environment variables or a Git-ignored .mcap-ops.local.json file:

{
  "host": "your-ssh-alias",
  "destination": "/absolute/path/to/mcap-ops"
}

These are placeholders, not a working deployment. Alternatively set MCAP_OPS_TEST_HOST and MCAP_OPS_TEST_ROOT. Explicit sync CLI options take precedence, then environment variables, then local configuration. The project path must be absolute and contain no spaces or parent traversal. Never put credentials in this file; use normal SSH authentication.

Before each sync, compare HEAD and worktree changes on both sides. Do not overwrite other tasks' edits or divergent history. A matching HEAD alone does not prove the remote worktree is clean.

docs.title: Synchronize reviewed sources
docs.text:
git status --short
python3 scripts/sync_sources.py

The script preserves repository-relative paths and includes tracked and nonignored new files. It does not copy .git, delete files, advance Git history, or run tests. It updates same-name source files, so inspect the execution checkout first. Never add third-party showcase material, tooling, environments, private configuration, or binary artifacts to Git.

docs.title: Project-local tools
docs.text:
At the execution checkout's root:

export CARGO_HOME="$PWD/.tools/cargo"
export RUSTUP_HOME="$PWD/.tools/rustup"
export PATH="$CARGO_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export VIRTUAL_ENV="$PWD/.venv"
rustc --version
.venv/bin/python --version

This assumes the toolchain has been installed into those locations. For a new environment, follow getting started; do not borrow another training or robot-control project's environment.

cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked -j 12
cargo run --locked --release -p mcap-ops-core --example quality_pipeline
.venv/bin/maturin develop --release --locked
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests
.venv/bin/python examples/quickstart.py

For differential checking, profiling, and benchmarks, follow RSI. Do not rerun hundreds of historical candidates for an ordinary documentation change. Shared CI is not a controlled performance-acceptance environment. The workflow consists of runbooks and CLI tools; no GitHub Actions/self-hosted runner or SSH secret deployment is implied.

docs.title: Scope every change
docs.text:
• Operators: public types, error boundaries, generated fixtures, units, shapes, causality.
  • Python exports: bindings, wrapper, all, return types, public tests, API documentation.
  • Decoders: schemas, clocks, fields, unknown-encoding failures, limits, original ordering.
  • Optimizations: one hypothesis, comparable artifacts, separate accepted commits, rejected evidence.
  • Documentation: equivalent English/Chinese pages, working links/diagrams, executable snippets.

Workflow safety tests use temporary Git repositories. They cover separate series, decision preservation, stale-candidate rejection, owned-path restore, acceptance without implicit commit, invalid names, and minimum paired blocks.

docs.title: Commit and publish the execution checkout
docs.text:
Stage only related files and inspect the diff. Keep performance commits separate from documentation, scaffolding, and correctness fixes.

git diff --check
git diff --cached
# Commit the reviewed files; the worktree must then be clean.
python3 scripts/publish_remote.py

The publication tool transfers a Git bundle, validates tracked-file hashes and tree identity, checks unexpected untracked files, and requires a fast-forward. Committed deletions are moved into a local artifact backup only when the remote file still matches its prior committed bytes. Unexpected edits fail closed. A local receipt records the verified target; it is not published.

Never bypass divergent history with force/reset. After successful verification, push the authorized remote normally:

git push origin main

docs.title: Documentation and distribution
docs.text: README graphics are checked-in SVG, with Mermaid diagrams in the guides. There is no extra documentation-site build dependency. Maintain each English/Chinese pair together; shared raw measurements remain a single evidence source. Do not upload credentials, recordings, or third-party demonstration packages. Registry packages and release attachments are separate deliverables: a Git push does not publish an installable package.

docs.title: Building and Publishing the Documentation
docs.text: Public site: https://xieweikai.github.io/mcap-ops/. English is the default; Chinese lives under /zh/. The language selector keeps the current page. There are two entry points: Tutorials for learning and Documentation for operator/type lookup, plus the full RSI playbook.

docs.title: Build and validate
docs.text:
All build/test commands run at the repository root in the configured Linux execution environment. Use the local-only execution configuration described in contributing. Never publish deployment coordinates.

python3 -m venv .tools/docs
.tools/docs/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
export CARGO_HOME="$PWD/.tools/cargo"
export RUSTUP_HOME="$PWD/.tools/rustup"
export PATH="$CARGO_HOME/bin:$PATH"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests
.tools/docs/bin/python scripts/build_docs.py
.tools/docs/bin/python scripts/check_docs_site.py

build_docs.py uses strict MkDocs validation and rustdoc warnings-as-errors. It records the source revision and dirty state in build.json. A final scan rejects output containing execution-checkout or home-directory paths. The checked-in dependencies are documentation-only; the package has no new runtime dependencies.

For browser preview, serve .artifacts/docs/site from the execution environment and use an authorized local tunnel. Check desktop and mobile navigation, language switching on an inner page, English/Chinese search, code copying, Mermaid rendering, and Rust symbol links. Browser checks need Playwright and a project-local Chromium installation; they are optional development tools, not site build dependencies. See the runnable commands in check_docs_browser.py.

docs.title: Publish
docs.text:
1. Commit reviewed source locally. Synchronize via scripts/publish_remote.py and push main. Local, execution, and GitHub source revisions must agree.
  2. Build again in the clean execution checkout. Run the site checker and browser check. Copy only .artifacts/docs/site/ back to the same local artifact path.
  3. Run python3 scripts/publish_docs.py locally with gh authentication. It checks the clean source revision, complete artifact, and matching GitHub main; it commits static files in a disposable clone and pushes gh-pages without force. No build runs locally.
  4. In repository Settings > Pages, select Deploy from a branch, gh-pages, / (root) (one-time setup). .nojekyll keeps the already-built files intact. GitHub's native Pages deployment publishes the static branch; no custom CI runner needs access to the execution environment.
  5. Wait for the Pages deployment to succeed. Check build.json on the live site and test the actual /mcap-ops/ base path.

A newer source commit requires a fresh clean build; dirty/stale artifacts are refused. A concurrent gh-pages update causes a non-fast-forward failure rather than overwriting it. Review that update before retrying.

docs.title: Editing rules
docs.text:
• Add English and Chinese pages together, and include them in mkdocs.yml.
  • Every Python reference page has a real public signature and a runnable generated-fixture example. Tests compare signatures/defaults with the installed package and run both language versions.
  • Preserve Markdown-relative links so documents also work on GitHub.
  • Rustdoc is generated, not translated or edited by hand; bilingual conceptual pages explain the same types and link to the shared exact reference.
  • Keep history, source data, private artifacts, and execution coordinates out of the static branch. The README banner remains the shared vector asset.

Component Requirement or verified scope Python Package requirement: >=3.10; verified with CPython 3.12.3 NumPy Package requirement: >=1.24; final campaign used 2.5.4 Rust 1.90.0, pinned in rust-toolchain.toml Python build maturin >=1.9,<2; a working native compiler/linker MCAP and images Implemented through Rust dependencies; ROS is not required Video Caller-installed ffmpeg and ffprobe; explicit executable paths are supported Verified wheel Linux x86-64 / glibc 2.39+, cp310-abi3; macOS/Windows are not verified

No package has been published to PyPI or crates.io. Do not assume a similarly named registry package is this implementation. Keep full Git history when cloning: the RSI reference oracle materializes an older commit.

Maintainers author locally and execute builds/tests in a separate configured Linux environment, using project-local tools. The commands below run at the repository root on the chosen build environment; external users can build in their own controlled environment.

docs.title: Python from source
docs.text:
Make Rust 1.90.0 available, then run:

python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install "maturin>=1.9,<2" "numpy>=1.24" "pytest>=8"
.venv/bin/maturin develop --release --locked
.venv/bin/python examples/quickstart.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests

Expected example output:

linear: [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0]
previous: [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0]
quality: [('above_range', 1)]
history shape: (1, 3, 1)

The example uses generated arrays and assertions; it does not read recordings or start services.

docs.title: Build and install a wheel
docs.text:
.venv/bin/maturin build --release --locked --out dist
python3 -m venv .tools/consumer
.tools/consumer/bin/python -m pip install dist/*.whl
.tools/consumer/bin/python examples/quickstart.py

Keep only the intended wheel in dist/. The platform tag depends on the build environment. The historical verified wheel is retained in the artifact store under .artifacts/rsi/per-op10/wheel/; it is not tracked by Git and has not been published as a release attachment.

docs.title: Rust dependencies
docs.text:
In the consuming project's Cargo.toml, adapt these paths to your checkout:

[dependencies]
mcap-ops-core = { path = "../mcap-ops/crates/core" }
mcap-ops-io = { path = "../mcap-ops/crates/io" }

Array-only applications need only core. Run the complete repository example:

cargo run --locked --release -p mcap-ops-core --example quality_pipeline

It combines inspection, gating, interval selection, and resampling through public interfaces. See the Rust guide and example source.

docs.title: Operator Catalog · 0.1.0
docs.text:
Documentation · Python signatures · Rust interfaces

Sources are read-only. Transformations return new results without modifying an input MCAP or array in place. The Python column describes the actual public surface, not every capability available in Rust.

docs.title: 1. Time and alignment
docs.text: Rust interface Input → output Python require_strict Timestamps → strict-order validation or error Internal validation, not separately exported uniform_grid Bounds, rational rate, point cap → half-open target grid Same name; returns list inspect_time Original-order timestamps, gap threshold → clock/interval statistics Available through inspect_signal.time align_timestamps Ordered source/target, tolerances → indices, offsets, validity Same name map_clock Time, origin, offset, ppb → corrected timestamps Rust-only expand_batch_timestamps Message times, counts, offsets → sample times Rust-only

docs.title: 2. Quality inspection
docs.text:
Rust interface Input → output Python inspect_signal Signal, QualityConfig → statistics and Issue evidence Same name; NumPy inputs

Checks include non-finite values, ranges, clock reversals/duplicates/gaps, rate, acceleration, local Hampel spikes, and flatline candidates. Total counts survive detail truncation. Disorder marks dynamic checks incomplete instead of silently repairing time. Hampel's window is a radius on both sides and can consume future samples; it is an offline quality check.

docs.title: 3. Policy and intervals
docs.text: Rust interface Input → output Python gate QualityReport, GatePolicy → passed, reasons, flagged_fraction Rust-only IntervalSet::new Half-open intervals → sorted/merged set Rust-only contains / mask Time point/array → membership/mask Rust-only intersection / difference Two sets → intersection/difference Rust-only affected_centers Bad intervals, context lengths → affected centers Rust-only

docs.title: 4. Sampling and filtering
docs.text:
Rust interface Input → output Python resample Signal, target, SampleOptions → Sampled Same name history_windows Signal, centers, nonpositive offsets → Windowed Values are 3-D; masks remain flat ema Ordered Signal, tau seconds, gap → Filtered Same name lowpass_taps Rate/cutoff Hz, odd tap count → normalized coefficients Same name; returns list fir Regular signal, taps, mode, period/tolerance → Filtered Same name; valid is a list unwrap_angles Periodic signal, period, gap → unwrapped Signal Same name

Sampling supports previous, nearest, linear, and SLERP. Previous is causal and age-limited. Nearest may use future values only when allowed. Linear/SLERP require valid bracketing support within the gap limit. There is no automatic anti-aliasing. SLERP uses shortest-path xyzw interpolation with input norm within 0.01 of one. Filters do not bridge unsupported gaps.

docs.title: 5. MCAP and decoding
docs.text:
Rust interface Input → output Python RawReader Path, MessageFilter, ReadLimits → original-order message iterator Rust-only inspect_mcap Path, filter, limits, gap → channel/schema/clock/completion report Same name JsonSignalSpec::decode JSON message and field/clock specification → samples Through read_json_signal read_signal / SignalDecoder Path and explicit decoder → Signal Built-in JSON path via read_json_signal

Unknown CDR/Protobuf payloads need upstream adapters. Container readability does not establish payload support. Only present CRCs can be checked, and early iterator termination is not full-file validation. Source identity is checked at EOF; callers must keep the source unchanged during reading.

docs.title: Python API · 0.1.0
docs.text:
Documentation · Installation · Runnable example

Import mcap_ops as ops. This reference follows the actual wrapper and bindings. Do not depend on private _native entry points.

docs.title: Common inputs and outputs
docs.text:
• Timestamps, targets, centers, offsets: contiguous one-dimensional np.int64, in ns.
  • Values: one- or two-dimensional np.float64; two-dimensional shape is (N,D). Strided and reversed value views are supported.
  • Inputs are copied into Rust-owned snapshots; outputs do not alias or modify caller buffers.
  • Signal results contain timestamps (int64 array), values (float64 array), and channels (int).
  • Diagnostic reports are dictionaries. Some interfaces return lists, as documented below.
  • Bindings hold the GIL; episode-level process scheduling belongs upstream.

docs.title: 1. inspect_signal
docs.text:
ops.inspect_signal(timestamps, values, config=None) -> dict
Configuration field Default Units / meaning max_gap_ns int64 maximum Threshold for positive time gaps lower, upper None D finite thresholds in value units max_rate None D nonnegative thresholds in value-units/second max_acceleration None D nonnegative thresholds in value-units/second squared hampel_window_ns None Positive time radius on each side; may use future samples hampel_sigma 3.0 MAD multiplier hampel_min_deviation 0.0 Minimum absolute deviation in value units max_hampel_samples 4096 Per-window sample cap, at least 3 flatline_duration_ns None Flatline candidate duration flatline_tolerance 0.0 Numeric tolerance for flatline checks max_issues 10000 Stored issue-detail cap; total count remains available

Returns time/channel statistics, issues, total_issues, issues_truncated, flagged_sample_count, and dynamic_checks_completed. Codes are non_finite, below_range, above_range, clock_reversal, duplicate_time, gap, rate, acceleration, spike, and flatline. Threshold arrays must match D; scalars are not broadcast. The operator does not repair or delete data.

docs.title: 2. uniform_grid
docs.text:
ops.uniform_grid(start_ns, end_ns, rate_num, rate_den, max_points) -> list[int]

Constructs a half-open [start,end) integer-nanosecond grid at rate_num/rate_den Hz, including rates such as 30000/1001. Convert the returned list with np.asarray(..., dtype=np.int64) before passing it to numeric APIs. Invalid bounds/rates, excessive point counts, or rates beyond nanosecond resolution fail explicitly.

docs.title: 3. align_timestamps
docs.text:
ops.align_timestamps(source, target, *, nearest=False,
                     max_past_ns=0, max_future_ns=0) -> dict

Matches timestamps without interpolating values. Source must be strictly increasing and target nondecreasing. Returns indices (int64[M]), offsets_ns (int64[M], source minus target), and valid (bool[M]). By default only past samples are considered; nearest=True permits future candidates within their separate tolerance. Ties prefer the past. Invalid indices are -1; zero invalid offsets do not mean an actual match.

docs.title: 4. resample
docs.text:
ops.resample(timestamps, values, target, *, method="previous",
             max_gap_ns=0, max_age_ns=0, allow_future=False) -> dict

Methods: previous, nearest, linear, slerp. See contracts.

Field Type / shape timestamps int64 (M,) values float64 (M,D) channels Python int status uint8 (M,); 0 is valid, codes 1–6 describe failure valid bool (M,), status==0 source_left, source_right int64 (M,); -1 when invalid alpha float64 (M,) uses_future bool (M,)

Source must be strictly increasing; target nondecreasing. Interpolation checks max_gap, while single-sample support checks max_age. Exact matches need no future support. Missing support is not zero-filled. SLERP requires D=4 in xyzw order, with input norm within 0.01 of one.

docs.title: 5. history_windows
docs.text:
ops.history_windows(timestamps, values, centers, offsets, *, method="previous",
                    max_gap_ns=0, max_age_ns=0, allow_future=False) -> dict

Requests centers[i] + offsets[j]. Centers must be strictly increasing; offsets nonempty, strictly increasing, and nonpositive. Adds centers and offsets to the resample fields. Values have shape (T,W,D) and timestamps (T,W); valid/status/source/alpha/uses_future remain flat (T*W,). Reshape explicitly, for example result["valid"].reshape(T,W).

docs.title: 6–9. Filters and angles
docs.text:
ops.ema(timestamps, values, tau_seconds, max_gap_ns) -> dict
ops.lowpass_taps(sample_rate_hz, cutoff_hz, taps) -> list[float]
ops.fir(timestamps, values, taps, *, mode="causal",
        period_ns=1, tolerance_ns=0) -> dict
ops.unwrap_angles(timestamps, values, *, period=2*np.pi, max_gap_ns=0) -> dict

EMA/FIR return Signal fields plus valid (list[bool]), mode, lookahead_samples, and group_delay_samples (float or None). Unwrapping returns only Signal fields, without valid.

lowpass_taps requires an odd tap count in [3,4095] and 0 < cutoff < sample_rate/2. FIR accepts a contiguous one-dimensional float64 tap array of length 1–4095; centered mode additionally requires odd length. Require period_ns>0 and 0<=tolerance_ns<period_ns. Unsupported edges remain NaN rather than being padded.

coefficients = np.asarray(ops.lowpass_taps(200.0, 20.0, 31), dtype=np.float64)
# t200/x200 are caller-provided regular 200 Hz arrays.
filtered = ops.fir(t200, x200, coefficients, period_ns=5_000_000)
valid = np.asarray(filtered["valid"], dtype=bool)
# Symmetric causal 31-tap FIR: 15-sample delay; first 30 samples lack support.

docs.title: 10–11. MCAP
docs.text:
ops.inspect_mcap(path, *, filter=None, limits=None, max_gap_ns=0) -> dict
ops.read_json_signal(path, topic, fields, channels, *, filter=None, limits=None,
                     timestamp_pointer=None, publish_clock=False,
                     max_samples=10_000_000) -> dict

path is a string. fields is a list of RFC 6901 JSON pointers resolving to numbers or flat numeric arrays. Values flatten in field order and must total channels. The default output clock is log_time. An explicit timestamp_pointer must resolve to int64 nanoseconds; otherwise publish_clock selects the MCAP clock.

Configuration Fields and defaults filter topics=[] (all), start_ns=None, end_ns=None, publish_clock=False limits max_record_bytes=67108864, max_messages=10000000

filter.publish_clock independently selects the clock used for filtering. Choosing a payload timestamp does not change that filter clock. Read limits apply to the scan, not just selected messages; a large chunk can exceed the record limit. These limits are not total RSS bounds.

inspect_mcap returns source, file_bytes, scanned_messages, selected_messages, complete, crc_validation, filter, and channels. Channel entries contain topic, schema metadata/hash, and both clock statistics. The default gap threshold of zero counts every positive interval as a gap: set an appropriate threshold. Absent CRCs are not successful CRC checks; full-file completion requires EOF.

read_json_signal returns Signal fields. It does not decode CDR/Protobuf.

docs.title: 12–13. Images
docs.text:
ops.image_quality(data, options=None) -> dict
ops.transform_image(bytes, options_json=None, crop=None,
                    resize=None, filter="lanczos3") -> list[int]

data/bytes are compressed PNG/JPEG Python bytes. image_quality accepts an options dictionary; transform_image currently takes an options_json string, such as json.dumps(options). crop is [x,y,width,height]; resize is [width,height]. Filters: nearest, triangle, lanczos3. Output is a PNG integer list; use bytes() before saving or passing it on.

Default image options: max_width=16384, max_height=16384, max_pixels=64000000, dark_threshold=10, bright_threshold=245. Dimensions/limits must be valid and dark<bright. Metrics include dimensions, pixels, luminance_mean/std, dark_fraction, bright_fraction, laplacian_variance, and rgb_sha256. Laplacian variance is None for images smaller than 3×3. See media examples.

docs.title: 14. Video
docs.text:
ops.validate_video(path, *, ffmpeg="ffmpeg", ffprobe="ffprobe",
                   timeout_seconds=600.0) -> dict

Probes a local file, then completely decodes the first video stream. Returns complete, decoded, decoded_frames, elapsed_seconds, and probe. The total timeout budget is in (0,86400] seconds; each tool has a 2 MiB diagnostic limit. Missing tools, timeout, error diagnostics, empty video, or incomplete decoding fail. Standalone probe_video is not exported to Python.

docs.text: gate, IntervalSet, map_clock, inspect_time, expand_batch_timestamps, RawReader, SignalDecoder, and standalone probe_video remain Rust-only. Python can obtain time-quality summaries through inspect_signal/inspect_mcap. ops.__version__ is a version string, not a processing operator.

docs.title: Use core directly
docs.text:
The complete asserted example is quality_pipeline.rs. Run in the repository root of the configured execution environment:

cargo run --locked --release -p mcap-ops-core --example quality_pipeline

use mcap_ops_core::{Signal, sampling::{resample, Method, SampleOptions}};

fn main() -> mcap_ops_core::Result<()> {
    let input = Signal::new(vec![0, 10], vec![0.0, 1.0], 1)?;
    let output = resample(&input, &[5], SampleOptions {
        method: Method::Linear,
        max_gap_ns: 10,
        max_age_ns: 10,
        allow_future: true,
    })?;
    assert_eq!(output.values, vec![0.5]);
    assert_eq!(output.source_left, vec![0]);
    Ok(())
}

The small timestamps are still nanoseconds; do not mix milliseconds or seconds.

docs.text:
Module Public types and functions crate root Signal, SignalSpec, SignalKind, Error, Result time require_strict, uniform_grid, map_clock, inspect_time, align_timestamps, expand_batch_timestamps, TimeStats, TimeAlignment quality QualityConfig, QualityReport, Issue, IssueCode, ChannelStats, inspect_signal, GatePolicy, GateDecision, gate sampling Method, SampleOptions, Status, Sampled, Windowed, resample, history_windows selection Interval, IntervalSet filter FilterMode, Filtered, ema, lowpass_taps, fir, unwrap_angles

docs.title: Explicit gating and selection
docs.text:
use mcap_ops_core::quality::{gate, GatePolicy, IssueCode};
use mcap_ops_core::selection::{Interval, IntervalSet};

// report comes from inspect_signal; policy is an explicit caller choice.
let decision = gate(&report, &GatePolicy {
    reject_codes: vec![IssueCode::NonFinite, IssueCode::ClockReversal],
    max_flagged_fraction: 0.01,
    min_samples: 100,
})?;

let keep = IntervalSet::new(vec![Interval { start_ns: 0, end_ns: 1_000_000_000 }])?;
let bad = IntervalSet::new(vec![Interval { start_ns: 200_000_000, end_ns: 300_000_000 }])?;
let clean = keep.difference(&bad);
let selected = clean.mask(&target_times);

This fragment expects caller-provided report and target_times. new() merges overlapping/adjacent intervals; intersection/difference return new sets; mask also accepts unordered times. affected_centers(history_ns,future_ns) expands bad intervals to centers whose context touches them. Issue.last_ns is inclusive, so converting it into a half-open interval requires an explicit discrete-sample coverage policy and overflow handling.

docs.title: IO and decoders
docs.text:
use mcap_ops_io::mcap_ops::{RawReader, MessageFilter, ReadLimits};

for message in RawReader::open("example.mcap", MessageFilter::default(), ReadLimits::default())? {
    let message = message?;
    println!("{} {}", message.channel.topic, message.log_time);
}

RawReader preserves file order. Breaking early does not validate the whole file; CRC/EOF/source-identity checks require their corresponding read stages. Do not modify or truncate a source while reading it.

The decoder boundary is:

pub trait SignalDecoder {
    fn channels(&self) -> usize;
    fn decode(&self, message: &mcap::Message<'_>)
        -> mcap_ops_io::Result<Vec<mcap_ops_io::mcap_ops::DecodedSample>>;
}

Adapters match topic/schema, decode fields, define clock and units, expand batched samples, and return the declared channel count. Unrelated messages return an empty Vec; malformed relevant messages return an error, not a silent skip. Custom adapters referring directly to mcap types need a compatible mcap = "0.26" dependency.

Call read_signal(path, filter, limits, &decoder, max_samples) to collect a Signal. Built-in JsonSignalSpec contains topic, fields, channels, timestamp_pointer, and publish_clock. CDR/Protobuf adapters are not built in. If upstream already has arrays, bypass IO entirely.

docs.title: Container and payload are separate boundaries
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    M["MCAP container"] --> RAW["Raw messages + schema + clocks"]
    RAW --> N["Explicit numeric schema decoder"]
    RAW --> V["Upstream image / video payload extraction"]
    N --> S["Signal / NumPy"]
    V --> I["image_quality / transform_image"]
    V --> F["Local video file<br/>validate_video"]

A readable container does not imply an understood payload. JSON numeric extraction is built in; CDR/Protobuf, compressed-image schemas, video packet assembly, and packet timestamps belong to upstream adapters.

docs.title: Inspect and extract JSON
docs.text:
Suppose topic /state has message_encoding=json and payload {"t_ns":10000000,"position":[0.1,0.2,0.3]}:

import mcap_ops as ops

path = "/data/example.mcap"  # Replace with your read-only source.
inventory = ops.inspect_mcap(
    path,
    filter={"topics": ["/state"]},
    limits={"max_record_bytes": 64*1024*1024, "max_messages": 1_000_000},
    max_gap_ns=100_000_000,
)
signal = ops.read_json_signal(
    path, topic="/state", fields=["/position"], channels=3,
    filter={"topics": ["/state"]},
    timestamp_pointer="/t_ns",
    max_samples=1_000_000,
)
print(signal["values"].shape)  # (N, 3)

Pointers such as /pose/position/0 follow RFC 6901; escape keys containing / or ~. Missing/nonnumeric fields, wrong channel counts, and invalid timestamps fail rather than silently skipping messages. Without timestamp_pointer, output uses log_time, or publish_time if publish_clock=True. filter.publish_clock separately selects the clock used for filtering.

Reading preserves file order and validates present chunk/data/summary CRCs. Zero CRC means absent, not passed. Early RawReader termination is not whole-file validation, and sources must remain unchanged while open.

max_record_bytes limits records, max_messages limits the scan, and max_samples limits decoded output. They are not total-memory limits: decompression, timestamp statistics, and collected values consume additional memory.

docs.title: Image metrics and transformation
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
import json
import mcap_ops as ops

raw = Path("frame.jpg").read_bytes()
limits = {"max_width": 4096, "max_height": 4096, "max_pixels": 16_000_000}
quality = ops.image_quality(raw, options=limits)

# crop=[x,y,width,height] must fit; resize does not preserve aspect ratio automatically.
png = bytes(ops.transform_image(
    raw, options_json=json.dumps(limits),
    resize=[224, 224], filter="lanczos3",
))
# New PNG data; the caller decides whether and where to save it.

Mean/std use weighted RGB luminance. Dark/bright fractions are threshold statistics; Laplacian variance can inform blur review but has no universal cross-scene pass threshold. rgb_sha256 compares decoded dimensions and RGB content, not original file bytes or semantic similarity across viewpoints.

Only PNG/JPEG are supported. transform_image returns list[int], requiring bytes() for byte consumers. Resizing changes pixels; lossless PNG encoding does not imply that resizing preserves the original image.

docs.title: Video integrity
docs.text:
video = ops.validate_video(
    "/data/episode.mp4",
    ffmpeg="ffmpeg", ffprobe="ffprobe", timeout_seconds=120.0,
)
assert video["complete"] and video["decoded"]
print(video["decoded_frames"])

External tools receive argument arrays, not shell fragments. The adapter accepts local files, probes, and completely decodes the first video stream. Timeout, error diagnostics, missing frames, or a missing completion marker fail. Success does not certify visual meaning, audio integrity, or return frame arrays.

For model synchronization, retain frame timestamps, select indices with align_timestamps, then process the selected frames. Average FPS cannot reconstruct exact capture times.

docs.title: Choose semantics before a sampling method
docs.text:
Signal Possible processing Explicit policy Continuous position linear; previous for causal observations Units, support gap, future permission Commands/modes previous Validity age and treatment of stale commands Quaternions slerp xyzw, norm requirements, frame Force/IMU High-frequency history or lowpass then downsample Bandwidth, latency, preservation of impacts Images align_timestamps selects frame indices Maximum frame age; never index invalid -1 Events Preserve event time and aggregate upstream Continuous interpolation may be inappropriate

These are composition choices, not hidden library policy. Signals must first share comparable clocks. Similar numbers do not establish a common clock. map_clock is currently Rust-only and requires explicit correction parameters.

flowchart TB
    P["Position 100 Hz"] --> Q["Inspect original ordering"]
    W["Force 200 Hz"] --> Q
    C["Camera about 30 Hz"] --> Q
    Q --> POLICY["Upstream review / Segmentation / Clock interpretation"]
    POLICY --> GRID["Target timeline 50 Hz"]
    GRID --> POS["Position (T,D)"]
    GRID --> FORCE["Force history (T,4,D)"]
    GRID --> IMAGE["Past-frame indices (T,)"]

docs.title: Runnable example
docs.text:
These arrays are generated. Replace them with decoded observations without changing their unit and shape contracts.

import numpy as np
import mcap_ops as ops

ms = 1_000_000
joint_t = np.arange(0, 101, 10, dtype=np.int64) * ms
joint_x = np.column_stack([joint_t / 1e9, joint_t / 1e9 * 2]).astype(np.float64)
force_t = np.arange(0, 101, 5, dtype=np.int64) * ms
force_x = np.ones((len(force_t), 6), dtype=np.float64)
frame_t = np.array([0, 33, 67, 100], dtype=np.int64) * ms

grid = np.asarray(ops.uniform_grid(20*ms, 101*ms, 50, 1, 100), dtype=np.int64)
report = ops.inspect_signal(joint_t, joint_x, {"max_gap_ns": 15*ms})
assert report["total_issues"] == 0

joint = ops.resample(joint_t, joint_x, grid, method="previous", max_age_ns=15*ms)
force = ops.history_windows(
    force_t, force_x, grid,
    np.array([-15, -10, -5, 0], dtype=np.int64) * ms,
    max_age_ns=5*ms,
)
frames = ops.align_timestamps(frame_t, grid, max_past_ns=40*ms)

force_valid = force["valid"].reshape(len(grid), 4).all(axis=1)
step_valid = joint["valid"] & force_valid & frames["valid"]
assert joint["values"].shape == (5, 2)
assert force["values"].shape == (5, 4, 6)
assert step_valid.all()

Image matching selects indices, not interpolated compressed bytes. Check frames.valid before indexing. Several model steps may reuse one frame.

docs.title: Quality selection
docs.text:
Python can use reports for business decisions, but gate/IntervalSet are currently Rust-only. Use Rust or an explicit upstream policy for interval operations. Truncated issue detail is not a complete bad-sample mask.

Impacts, contact, and long periods of stillness can be desired behavior. Define which codes reject an episode, which require review, and whether bad intervals invalidate history-window centers.

Do not filter values by step_valid and fabricate a continuous timeline. Preserve the mask or split into contiguous valid episodes with original time and provenance.

docs.title: Downsampling and delay
docs.text:
resample is not an anti-aliasing filter. For regular high-rate signals, use lowpass_taps and fir before downsampling supported segments. When converting 200 Hz to 50 Hz, choose a cutoff below the new 25 Hz Nyquist limit, based on the signal bandwidth. A symmetric causal 31-tap FIR delays the signal by 15 input steps, or 75 ms; centered mode instead needs 75 ms of lookahead.

Training features must obey deployment causality. Equal output timestamps do not automatically compensate for processing delay.

docs.title: Upstream persistence
docs.text: Retain source identity, topics/fields/units, clock source and mapping, operator version/configuration, original and target timestamps, valid/status, source_left/right/alpha, and segmentation policy. The library does not include a dataset writer; the consuming pipeline owns serialization.

docs.title: Rust-only interfaces
docs.text:
gate, IntervalSet, map_clock, inspect_time, expand_batch_timestamps, RawReader, SignalDecoder, and standalone probe_video have no Python export. map_clock applies caller-provided parameters; it does not fit clocks.

Interface Inputs and output Behavior and errors require_strict &[i64] -> Result<()> Empty/singleton input passes; duplicates or reversals return Invalid inspect_time times, nonnegative max_gap_ns -> TimeStats Inspect original order; summarize only positive intervals, with interpolated median/p95; estimated_hz is 1e9/median; unavailable statistics are None map_clock times, origin, offset (ns), rate_ppb -> Vec<i64> Apply origin + round((t-origin)*(1+rate_ppb/1e9)) + offset; scale must be positive; half ties round away from zero; checked int64 output expand_batch_timestamps message_times, counts, flat offsets (ns) -> Vec<i64> One count per message; sum(counts) equals offsets.len(); add each message time to its offsets with checked arithmetic gate &QualityReport, &GatePolicy -> GateDecision Reject too few samples, excess flagged fraction, or any rejected code; full internal flags survive detail truncation; fraction is 0 for empty input IntervalSet normalized half-open intervals -> sets / masks See method contracts; invalid spans or overflowing context expansion fail RawReader::open path, filter, limits -> fallible message iterator Preserve file order and CRC/error handling; early termination does not validate EOF or the complete source read_signal path, filter, limits, &dyn SignalDecoder, max_samples -> Signal Collect decoded samples within a positive cap; validate channels; retain order; malformed relevant messages or no decoded samples fail decode PNG/JPEG bytes, &ImageOptions -> image::DynamicImage Check format, dimensions, pixels and allocation limits before returning a decoded image probe_video local path, ffprobe executable, Duration -> serde_json::Value Require video streams and clean tool completion within a bounded timeout; no frame decoding or quality certification

map_clock returns new timestamps; it does not overwrite source clocks, sort, deduplicate, or guarantee that rounding preserves strict ordering. Store the mapping parameters and retain original times. Batch expansion likewise does not guess sampling frequency or enforce global ordering.

docs.title: Signal and SignalSpec
docs.text:
Type Purpose / contract Signal Owned Vec<i64> nanosecond timestamps, row-major Vec<f64> values, positive channel count Signal::new Validates timestamps.len() * channels == values.len(); does not enforce ordering or finiteness Signal::require_ordered Validates strict timestamp ordering explicitly Signal::timestamps / values / row Borrow slices; row(index) requires an in-range index Signal::len / is_empty / channels Inspect shape without copying Signal::into_parts Consumes the signal and transfers (timestamps, row-major values, channels) without copying SignalSpec name, kind, channels, unit, frame, timestamp_source, required SignalKind Continuous, QuaternionXyzw, Command, Discrete, Event

SignalSpec is descriptive metadata, not an automatic dispatch or conversion engine. Python Signal dictionaries contain timestamps: int64[N], values: float64[N,D], and channels: int. Metadata remains upstream.

docs.title: Quality reports and policies
docs.text:
Type Fields / meaning TimeStats samples, first_ns, last_ns, reversals, duplicates, gaps, positive_interval_min/median/p95/max_ns, estimated_hz ChannelStats finite, nonfinite, min, max, mean, std, statistics_overflow Issue code, channel, start_index, end_index_exclusive, start_ns, last_ns, metric, threshold QualityReport time, channels, issues, total_issues, issues_truncated, dynamic_checks_completed, flagged_sample_count QualityConfig Detection thresholds and resource caps; complete defaults GatePolicy reject_codes, max_flagged_fraction in [0,1], min_samples GateDecision passed, reasons, flagged_fraction

Unavailable statistics are None. Issue.channel may be None for time issues. There is no severity field. Its index span is half-open, but last_ns is the inclusive last source timestamp.

IssueCode serializes as non_finite, below_range, above_range, clock_reversal, duplicate_time, gap, rate, acceleration, spike, or flatline. gate uses full internal flags/codes even when issue detail is truncated. Python reports exclude flagged_samples and all_codes; use the complete counts or an explicit upstream policy, not a reconstructed partial mask.

docs.title: SampleOptions, Sampled, Windowed, and Status
docs.text:
SampleOptions has method, max_gap_ns, max_age_ns, allow_future. Method is Previous, Nearest, Linear, or Slerp. Limits are explicit in Rust; Python sampling defaults both limits to zero.

Field Python Sampled Python Windowed timestamps int64 (M,) int64 (T,W) values float64 (M,D) float64 (T,W,D) channels int int centers, offsets absent int64 (T,), (W,) status uint8 (M,) uint8 (T*W,) valid bool (M,) bool (T*W,) source_left/right int64 (M,) int64 (T*W,) alpha float64 (M,) float64 (T*W,) uses_future bool (M,) bool (T*W,)

Rust uses flat vectors and Windowed.samples, with centers/offsets describing shape. Source indices refer to the passed signal, not raw file message IDs. Single-sample support repeats one index with alpha=0. Validity applies to the complete row, not individual channels.

Code Rust Status Meaning 0 Valid Supported, finite row 1 Missing Required support absent 2 Gap Two-point support interval exceeds limit 3 Stale Single-point support exceeds age limit 4 NonFinite Nonfinite input/output 5 Future Future support forbidden 6 InvalidQuaternion Quaternion fails norm requirements

Invalid outputs use NaN values/alpha and source indices -1. Consult status; do not infer failure type from NaN alone. valid is exactly status == 0.

docs.title: TimeAlignment and Filtered
docs.text:
TimeAlignment contains indices, offsets_ns (source minus target), and valid. It selects samples without changing their values.

Filtered contains a Signal, valid, mode, lookahead_samples, and group_delay_samples. Python flattens Signal fields into the result dictionary; its valid remains a list, not an ndarray. FilterMode is Causal/Centered. Unknown constant group delay is None; a zero reported delay does not imply zero lookahead.

docs.title: Interval and IntervalSet
docs.text: Interval { start_ns, end_ns } represents [start,end). IntervalSet::new rejects empty/reversed intervals, sorts them, and merges overlaps/adjacency. intervals borrows the normalized spans. contains, mask, intersection, and difference query/select without changing source data. mask accepts unordered times. affected_centers(history_ns,future_ns) expands bad intervals to centers whose context touches them, with overflow checks. These APIs are Rust-only.

docs.title: mcap_ops.align_timestamps
docs.text:
Match timestamps to source indices without interpolating values.

mcap_ops.align_timestamps(source, target, *, nearest=False, max_past_ns=0, max_future_ns=0)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning source int64[N] required Contiguous, strictly increasing, ns. target int64[M] required Contiguous, nondecreasing, ns. nearest bool False Permit future candidates; otherwise match past only. max_past_ns / max_future_ns int 0 Nonnegative, separate past/future tolerances, ns.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: dict: indices int64[M], offsets_ns int64[M] (source minus target), valid bool[M]. Invalid indices are -1 and invalid offsets are 0.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: ValueError for noncontiguous/wrong dtype arrays, unordered timestamps, or negative tolerances. OverflowError if an offset cannot fit int64.

docs.title: Semantics and boundaries
docs.text:
Ties prefer the past. A zero invalid offset is not an exact match. Check valid before indexing frames: Python index -1 otherwise selects the last frame. This matches already comparable clocks; it does not estimate clock drift.

Numeric inputs follow the common contracts: no implicit dtype conversion, contiguous time arrays, copied inputs with no mutation. Python/PyO3 conversion can also raise TypeError or OverflowError.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import mcap_ops as ops

t = np.array([0, 10, 20], dtype=np.int64) * 1_000_000
x = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0], dtype=np.float64)
target = np.array([5, 15, 30], dtype=np.int64) * 1_000_000
r = ops.align_timestamps(t, target, max_past_ns=6_000_000)
assert r["indices"].tolist() == [0, 1, -1]
assert r["valid"].tolist() == [True, True, False]

docs.title: mcap_ops.ema
docs.text:
Apply a causal, time-aware exponential moving average.

mcap_ops.ema(timestamps, values, tau_seconds, max_gap_ns)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning timestamps int64[N] required Contiguous 1-D source timestamps, nanoseconds. values float64[N] or [N,D] required Numeric samples; strided views accepted. tau_seconds float required Finite positive time constant in seconds. max_gap_ns int required Nonnegative reset threshold in nanoseconds.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Filtered dictionary: Signal fields plus valid list[bool], mode="causal", lookahead_samples=0, group_delay_samples=None. Values retain shape (N,D).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: ValueError for unordered time, invalid shape, nonpositive/nonfinite tau, or negative gap.

docs.title: Semantics and boundaries
docs.text:
Weight is 1-exp(-dt/tau). A gap beyond the threshold resets state to the current finite row. Any nonfinite channel invalidates the row and resets all-channel state; the next finite row restarts it. No future samples are used; EMA has no single constant group delay.

Numeric inputs follow the common contracts: no implicit dtype conversion, contiguous time arrays, copied inputs with no mutation. Python/PyO3 conversion can also raise TypeError or OverflowError.

assert r["valid"] == [True, True, True]
assert 0.0 < r["values"][1, 0] < 1.0
assert r["lookahead_samples"] == 0

docs.title: mcap_ops.fir
docs.text:
Filter regular-grid samples with explicitly bounded support.

mcap_ops.fir(timestamps, values, taps, *, mode="causal", period_ns=1, tolerance_ns=0)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning timestamps int64[N] required Contiguous 1-D source timestamps, nanoseconds. values float64[N] or [N,D] required Numeric samples; strided views accepted. taps float64[K] required Contiguous finite coefficients, 1 <= K <= 4095. mode str "causal" causal or centered; centered requires odd K. period_ns int 1 Positive expected input period, ns. tolerance_ns int 0 0 <= tolerance < period; spacing tolerance, ns.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Filtered dictionary: timestamps int64[N], values float64[N,D], channels, valid list[bool], mode, lookahead_samples, group_delay_samples (float or None).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: ValueError for unordered time, invalid taps, period/tolerance, or centered even-length coefficients. Irregular/missing support invalidates affected outputs.

docs.title: Semantics and boundaries
docs.text:
Causal output i is sum(taps[k] * x[i-k]). Centered mode shifts output by floor(K/2). Edges are not padded; gaps and nonfinite rows reset support. Symmetric causal taps report (K-1)/2 delay; asymmetric causal taps report None. Centered delay is 0 with K//2 lookahead.

Numeric inputs follow the common contracts: no implicit dtype conversion, contiguous time arrays, copied inputs with no mutation. Python/PyO3 conversion can also raise TypeError or OverflowError.

r = ops.fir(t, x, np.array([0.5, 0.5], dtype=np.float64), period_ns=10_000_000)
assert r["valid"] == [False, True, True]
np.testing.assert_allclose(r["values"][1:, 0], [0.5, 1.5])
assert r["group_delay_samples"] == 0.5

docs.title: mcap_ops.inspect_mcap
docs.text:

mcap_ops.inspect_mcap(path, *, filter=None, limits=None, max_gap_ns=0)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Meaning path str required Path to a regular local MCAP file. filter dict or None None MessageFilter: exact topics and a half-open time interval. limits dict or None None ReadLimits: record-byte and scanned-message caps. max_gap_ns int 0 Positive-interval gap threshold for both clock summaries, ns.

import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from mcap.writer import Writer
import mcap_ops as ops

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "example.mcap"
    with path.open("wb") as stream:
        writer = Writer(stream)
        writer.start()
        channel = writer.register_channel("/sensor", "json", 0)
        for i in range(3):
            writer.add_message(channel, i*10_000_000, json.dumps({"value": float(i)}).encode(), i*10_000_000)
        writer.finish()
    r = ops.inspect_mcap(str(path), max_gap_ns=15_000_000)
    assert r["complete"] and r["selected_messages"] == 3
    assert r["channels"][0]["topic"] == "/sensor"

docs.title: RSI: Evidence-Driven Iterative Optimization
docs.text:
Project overview · Documentation

This directory turns the repository's RSI method into versioned runbooks, command entry points, acceptance rules, and experiment templates. Execution reuses scripts/; evidence stays under docs/performance/. There is no duplicate runner or dependency on a particular assistant or skill system.

flowchart LR
    E["Read history and real callers"] --> P["Profile accepted baseline"]
    P --> H["State a falsifiable bottleneck hypothesis"]
    H --> C["Make one small change"]
    C --> V{"Correctness passes?"}
    V -->|"No"| R["Archive failure / Restore owned paths"]
    V -->|"Yes"| B["At least four AB/BA benchmark blocks"]
    B --> G{"Performance / Resource / Complexity gates pass?"}
    G -->|"No"| R
    G -->|"Yes"| A["Separate commit / Promote accepted baseline"]
    R --> E
    A --> E
    A --> F["Integration / Installed wheel / Publication"]

docs.title: Playbook
docs.text:
Document Contents workflow.md Preparation, exploration, baseline, trial, decision, commit, delivery profiling.md What to profile, Callgrind/cProfile, timing, noise, confirmations correctness.md Public contracts, immutable oracle, boundary cases, resource/complexity gates evidence.md All 380 decisions, successful and failed ideas, archive layout, script roles Campaign template Freeze scope, environment, workloads, and budget before exploration Experiment template Hypothesis, change, measurements, checks, decision, lesson

Every page and template has a matching Chinese version. Measurements and patches are shared evidence rather than language-specific copies.

docs.title: Acceptance rules
docs.text:
• At least four alternating AB/BA blocks, seven calibrated samples per side, with the same environment, CPU affinity, toolchain, flags, and fixtures.
  • Every block's geometric-mean latency reduction over the frozen case set is at least 8%.
  • No representative case's paired median regresses by more than 3%.
  • Correctness, errors, clocks, provenance, shapes, ownership, and limits remain intact; the added complexity must be justified.
  • PNG encoder candidates preserve decoded pixels and keep the largest measured output-size ratio at or below 1.25x.
  • Each accepted candidate gets a separate commit recording the method, before/after ns/op, worst block, correctness, and evidence paths.

Starting a process, compiling, or observing one fast sample does not complete an experiment. Rejected code does not remain in production; its evidence does. Compilation repairs and interrupted retries do not count as extra optimization rounds.

docs.title: Execution environment
docs.text:
Author, review, decide, and commit locally. Build, test, profile, and time in a separately configured Linux x86-64 checkout with project-local tools. The reference environment records hardware and software, not a deployment address. Keep target coordinates in ignored configuration. Benchmark trials run serially with fixed CPU affinity, without touching unrelated recordings, system profiler permissions, or robotics services.

Use a new series and globally unique label for a new campaign. Preserve initial, extension, and per-op10. The manual trial/decide/archive workflow supports new namespaces; the historical fixed-count runners are not general campaign engines.

docs.title: Immutable oracle and numeric rules
docs.text:
The reference implementation is commit 66248dacb608859d2cbd0f9f27227c65013a8027. prepare_reference.py materializes it into an isolated workspace and refuses changed reference sources. Full history is required; a missing reference commit is not a passing differential check.

  • Timestamps, indices, masks, statuses, counts, and discrete values match exactly.
  • Rust finite-value tolerance is abs(new-old) <= 1e-10 * (1 + abs(old)).
  • Python uses rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10, equal_nan=True, checking dtype/shape/container types.
  • Preserve observable NaN/Inf behavior; do not compare integers through lossy floats.
  • Diagnostics, exception types/messages, dictionary order, input immutability, and lack of output/input aliases are part of the interface.
  • Encoded image bytes may differ, but decoded dimensions/pixels must agree; image metrics use the declared numeric tolerance.

If an operator needs a different tolerance, justify and review it before looking at failed results. The oracle is not mathematical truth: fix discovered baseline bugs separately, rather than changing semantics and removing failing checks inside a supposedly equivalent optimization.

docs.title: Execute checks
docs.text:
At the configured execution checkout root, with project-local tool paths active:

cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked -j 12
python3 scripts/prepare_reference.py
CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=0 CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/target/reference" \
  cargo run --offline --release --manifest-path .artifacts/rsi/validation/Cargo.toml -j 12
.venv/bin/maturin develop --release --locked
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests

Offline execution requires cached dependencies. A missing cache is an environment preparation failure, not a successful oracle run. Bridge changes additionally need:

.venv/bin/python scripts/check_python_equivalence.py \
  --before .artifacts/rsi/python/accepted \
  --after .artifacts/rsi/python/CANDIDATE_LABEL

docs.title: Resource and maintenance gates
docs.text:
Concern Required evidence Temporary storage Peak bytes or a clear bound, such as another 8ND bytes for transposition Caches Capacity, complete key, invalidation, empty/singleton overhead Encoding Exact decoded pixels, size pairs per fixture, maximum ratio <=1.25 Complexity Production diff, new branches/helpers, duplicated algorithms, edge-case burden Dependencies/unsafe/approximation Not an implicit tradeoff; require separate design and review

PNG candidates enable --png-size-gate, which consumes oracle resource_png records. The size bound covers tested fixtures, not all future images. There is no universal automatic RSS gate: record analysis or measurement instead of claiming unmeasured cost is zero.

Line count alone is insufficient. A cryptic one-liner can cost more to maintain than a clear loop. Retain changes only when stable gains, applicable distributions, and maintenance cost are understood.

docs.title: Final artifact gate
docs.text:
Individually passing changes can regress in an integrated binary. Rebuild the campaign baseline and final source with the same final harness and run all representative workloads. Compare real release wheels, install into an isolated environment, and retain wheel/extension/source SHA-256 identities.

The historical verification record contains 36 Rust tests, five Python smoke tests, 291 interface comparisons, and the reference oracle. Later tests change current counts; report actual executions rather than repeating historical counts as if newly measured.
